questions.question_text: Jamal deposits $\$3200$ into a savings account paying $4\%$ p.a. simple interest. How much simple interest is earned in $5$ years?

options.why: Gave the total amount $P + I$ instead of the interest asked for.
Worked out one year's interest and forgot to multiply by the $5$ years.
Wrote $4\%$ as $0.004$, shifting the decimal point one place too far.

questions.question_text: Owen borrows $\$6000$ from a credit union to pay his course fees. Simple interest is charged at $9\%$ p.a. for $8$ months. How much interest is charged?

options.why: Substituted $n = 8$ as if the $8$ months were $8$ years against the annual rate.
Calculated a full year's interest and ignored the $8$-month term.
Divided the yearly interest by $12$ but then forgot to multiply by the $8$ months.

questions.question_text: Wally deposits $\$15\,000$ into a savings account paying $6\%$ p.a. simple interest for $3$ years. What is the total amount in the account at the end of the $3$ years?

options.why: Stopped at the interest and never added the principal back on.
Added only one year's interest to the principal instead of three years' interest.
Counted the principal twice, working out $P + P + I$ instead of $P + I$.

questions.question_text: Joy deposits $\$2800$ into a savings account paying $3.5\%$ p.a. simple interest. How long will it take to earn $\$490$ in interest? Give your answer in years.

options.why: Solved for $n$ correctly but labelled it months; an annual rate makes $n$ a number of years.
Used $1\%$ of the principal ($\$28$) as the yearly interest instead of $3.5\%$.
Substituted the rate as $3.5$ rather than converting $3.5\%$ to $0.035$.

questions.question_text: A savings account paying $9\%$ p.a. simple interest earned $\$129.60$ over $2$ years. How much was deposited at the start?

options.why: Divided by the rate but multiplied by the $2$ years instead of dividing by them.
Divided the interest by the $2$ years only and never divided by the rate.
Substituted the rate as $9$ instead of $0.09$ when dividing.

questions.question_text: Harry left $\$13\,000$ in a savings account for $4$ years and earned $\$1092$ in simple interest. What was the annual simple interest rate?

options.why: Divided the interest by the principal only, leaving out the $4$ years.
Attached the percent sign to the decimal without multiplying by $100$.
Multiplied the decimal $0.021$ by $100$ twice when converting to a percentage.
Read the line at $2$ years instead of at $3$ years.
Read the value at the end of the drawn line ($5$ years) rather than at $3$ years.
Read the interest for a single year rather than the total after $3$ years.

questions.question_text: Polly borrows $\$11\,000$ from a credit union and repays the loan in full at the end of $2$ years with a single payment of $\$12\,000$. What annual simple interest rate was she charged? Give your answer correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Divided the interest by the principal but left out the $2$ years.
Used the repayment $\$12\,000$ as the principal instead of the amount borrowed.
Treated the whole repayment as the interest instead of using $I = A - P$.

questions.question_text: Lynne deposits $\$1000$ into a savings account for a term of $15$ months. Simple interest is paid at $3.75\%$ p.a. How much will the investment be worth at the end of the term? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

options.why: Gave the interest earned instead of the total value of the investment.
Used $n = 1$ year and ignored the extra $3$ months of the term.
Substituted $n = 15$ instead of converting the $15$ months to $1.25$ years.
Rounded down to the whole-year gridline instead of reading the half-year mark.
Read across from $\$275$, one gridline above the required $\$225$.
Treated the dollar value as the reading on the time axis rather than tracing across to the line.
